original_question: Extend the theory of equivariant map superalgebras by allowing more general target Lie superalgebras, replacing the coordinate algebra A by a supercommutative algebra so that X becomes a superscheme, and replacing Gamma by a Z2-graded group. Determine the resulting representation theory in this broader super setting.
target_in_paper: Section 4.1(c), "Superschemes and superalgebras," read together with the existing classification result for equivariant map superalgebras in Theorem 3.12.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the exact trio of super-generalizations named in the paper: allowing more general target Lie superalgebras, replacing the coordinate algebra A by a supercommutative algebra so that X becomes a superscheme, and replacing Gamma by a Z2-graded group. It also correctly keeps the focus on representation theory, which is the surrounding theme of the paper and of the cited equivariant map superalgebra results.
missing_details: The paper's nearby concrete representation-theoretic benchmark is the classification of irreducible finite-dimensional modules, not the whole representation theory in full generality.
The target generalization in §4.1(c) is exemplified more specifically by taking g to be any finite-dimensional simple Lie superalgebra, not just an unspecified 'more general' target.
The ambient field for the superalgebra discussion in §§3-4 is an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0.

The starting object is an equivariant map superalgebra M(X,g)^Gamma with X = Spec A; in the generalized version A is to be replaced by a supercommutative algebra, i.e. X should be treated as a superscheme.

The current theory being generalized is Theorem 3.12: for basic classical targets, irreducible finite-dimensional modules are described by evaluation data when g_0 is semisimple, and by Kac-type generalized evaluation data in the type-I case.

The draft omits the hypotheses under which the known classification is proved in the survey's summary: g basic classical, A finitely generated, k algebraically closed, and Gamma acting freely on the rational points of X; the cited paper [Sav] is more restrictive still in assuming Gamma finite abelian.

The phrase 'Z2-graded group' is taken directly from §4.1(c), but the nearby text does not formally define it, so a stand-alone question should at least say that Gamma acts compatibly with the superscheme structure on X and the superalgebra structure on g.

The draft is broader than the paper-faithful formulation because it could be read as asking simultaneously for extensions, blocks, cohomology, Weyl modules, or infinite-dimensional categories, none of which are part of the specific open problem in §4.1(c).
refined_question: Over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic 0, generalize the equivariant map superalgebra setting of [Sav] by allowing the target g to be any finite-dimensional simple Lie superalgebra, the coordinate algebra A to be supercommutative (so X = Spec A is a superscheme), and Gamma to be a Z2-graded group acting compatibly on X and g. For the resulting generalized equivariant map superalgebra M(X,g)^Gamma, classify the irreducible finite-dimensional modules, and determine the correct analogue of the evaluation/generalized-evaluation (Kac-module) description of Theorem 3.12.
justification: The draft is clearly aiming at the open problem stated in §4.1(c), because that subsection lists exactly the three proposed super-extensions and no more. To keep the question faithful to the paper rather than broadening it, the right nearby context is the survey's summary of the existing equivariant map superalgebra classification in Theorem 3.12: that theorem is the precise representation-theoretic result available before the open problem, so the natural sharpened question is to extend that classification to the superized setting of §4.1(c), not to ask for an unrestricted 'full representation theory' of all such objects.
